article.overviewTitle: Manage S3 buckets and files in your browser
article.overview: S3 File Manager is an online file browser for Amazon S3 and S3-compatible object storage, including Cloudflare R2 and MinIO. Save multiple connections, switch between buckets, open folders, and filter objects in the current listing. Requests are signed in your browser and sent directly to your storage endpoint.
article.connectTitle: Connect Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, or MinIO
article.connect: Enter the provider’s S3 API endpoint, signing region, access key ID, and secret access key. For temporary credentials, enter the session token under Advanced settings. Cloudflare R2 uses the region auto. MinIO installations often use path-style addressing. If discovery is blocked or your key is scoped to specific buckets, enter their names in connection settings.
article.objectsTitle: Upload, download, and organize S3 objects
article.objects: Upload individual files or a folder and choose their destination path. Open object details to preview supported images and text, or edit small text files in place. Copy or move an object to another path or bucket on the same connection, or select several objects to delete at once. S3 folders are based on object key prefixes. To rename an object, move it to a new key.
article.corsTitle: Set up CORS for browser access to S3
article.cors: Open CORS setup above to copy a rule for the current origin. In Amazon S3, open the bucket’s Permissions tab and edit Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS). In Cloudflare R2, open the bucket’s Settings tab and edit CORS Policy. CORS controls which web origins can make requests. Your credentials still need permission for each S3 action.
article.credentialsTitle: Where are my connections and credentials saved?
article.credentials: Connection settings are stored in this browser. If you choose to remember credentials, the keys and session token are stored in this browser profile too. Leave that option off on shared devices. You can edit or remove a saved connection at any time.
